decisions.evidence: In dur114.png and s114 band1 line 1 the mark after יִשְׁעֵנוּ is a colon (two stacked dots), not a single period. Both דור words have a real vav with a dot on top between the dalet and the resh (holam male). They are not defective.
Band1 line 2: the vowel under the doubled yod is a three-dot cluster (segol) like the one under the mem. It is not a T-shaped qamatz. A colon follows.
Band1 line 3: there is no dot between עוֹלָמִים and עַל־אֲבוֹתֵינוּ, only a word space.
Band2 line 7 (מֶלֶךְ גּוֹ‑ל וּמוֹשִׁיעַ: מִמִּצְרַיִם): there are two stacked dots after וּמוֹשִׁיעַ.

Band2 last line and the full page: the marks under both the he and the resh have the same shape, each with a short vertical stem below the bar (qamatz). The mark under the resh does not look like a flat patah bar. The print is small, so this needs a zoom check if anyone disputes it.

decisions.exact_text: גָ?אָלְתָּ (no following punctuation; dagesh in the gimel not determinable)
decisions.evidence: Punctuation: band2 last line shows no period between גאלת and וְיַם־סוּף, so theirs is right on that point. Dagesh: at band resolution I cannot tell whether there is a dot inside the gimel. The gimel of גְּאַלְתָּנוּ at the start of the line above clearly has one, but this one is not clear. Drop the period. The dagesh needs a high-resolution crop.
Band3 line 1: there is a normal word space between וַיְכַסּוּ and מַיִם with no maqaf stroke. Compare the visible maqaf in עַל־זֹאת at the end of the same line.
Band3 line 4: the gimel of גדול has an interior dot, like the one in גֵּאִים in the same line.
Band3 line 4 and the full page: there is a dot inside the bowl of the final he (mappiq) and a patah below it.
Band3 line 7: the consonants are ו מ ב ר ך with no vertical vav between the bet and the resh. The holam is defective (a dot only). A period follows.

english115-egypt.png and band2 read 'From Egypt has Thou'. There is no t. Elsewhere on the page 'hast Thou' is printed correctly, so this is a source typo. Keep it literally and mark it sic 'has' / corr 'hast'.
english115-praises.png and band3 clearly read 'Praiscs'. Keep it literally and mark it sic 'Praiscs' / corr 'Praises'.

remaining_uncertainties.evidence: Not determinable at band or full-page resolution. Needs a high-resolution crop.
No interior dot is visible in band1 line 2. That probably means none is printed, but the print is small.
Band1 line 4: the dalets are too small to confirm or rule out a dot.

remaining_uncertainties.mark: tick above the lamed; no maqaf
remaining_uncertainties.evidence: The space and the missing maqaf are clear. There is a small stroke at the top right of the lamed of וְעַל. It looks like a print artifact or part of the letter, not a vowel or accent. Do not encode it.

remaining_uncertainties.mark: comma-like mark after the final he
remaining_uncertainties.evidence: Band1 line 6: a small tail is visible at the upper left of the he. It could be a printed comma or a stray mark. It is not inside the bowl, so it is not a mappiq. Isolate it as unresolved.
Band1 line 7: the mark looks like a flat bar (patah) next to the qamatz under the shin. It is small, so confidence is medium.
The dot is faint but appears to be present. Confidence is low to medium.

Band2 line 7 and the full page: between the vav and the lamed there is only a small fragment and a dot. The alef did not print. The word cannot be read from the pixels. Flag it for a check against the physical copy.
Band2 line 3: the dot above the vav is visible. Keep it as מִצְוֹ.
Band3 line 1: a small dot is visible above the zayin-alef area. Keep it as זֹאת. Confidence is medium.

remaining_uncertainties.mark: dagesh and shva on the vav
remaining_uncertainties.evidence: Band3 line 6: a dot inside the vav and a shva below it are visible. Confidence is medium.

notes: s115 'faith-/ful' is a hyphen at a line break (band1 lines 3-4), so joining it as 'faithful' is correct. 'awe-inspiring' has a real hyphen in mid-line (band3 line 5), so keep it.
The Divine Name on s114 is printed as the abbreviation יְיָ (band1 line 7, band2 line 8). This is consistent with the readings.
None of the four questions already sent to the human (junction rubric on 112, MiKhamokha on 116, זכרוננו/ופקדננו on 120, Jerusalem points on 124) fall on s114 or s115, so none were decided here.
The גָּאָלְתָּ decision is split: the punctuation is resolved in favour of theirs (no period), and the gimel dagesh is still unresolved.
